intro.data: A limit isn't just an object — it's an object with a PROMISE: from any consistent source there is exactly ONE map into it that makes everything line up. Here you must route a request through the joined row to its customer's region. Only one mediating map builds a consistent pair; the others force-fit a mismatched pair, and every downstream read then goes wrong. Find the one map that fits — and the faithful reads after it.
intro.alchemy: A limit is an object with a PROMISE: from any consistent source, exactly ONE map into it makes everything line up. Route the pairing through the matched pair to its reagent's grade. Only one mediating map builds a consistent pair; the others force-fit a mismatch, and every later read goes wrong. Find the one map that fits.
intro.spellcraft: A limit is an object with a PROMISE: from any consistent source, exactly ONE map into it makes everything line up. Route the binding through the matched pair to its ward's domain. Only one mediating map builds a consistent pair; the others force-fit a mismatch, and every later read goes wrong. Find the one map that fits.
intro.abstract: The universal property of the limit: any consistent cone factors through it by a UNIQUE mediating map. Build that map into the pullback and the faithful projections, so the value reaches the goal. Impostor mediating maps give inconsistent pairs.

afterSuccess.data: Only ONE mediating map built a key-consistent joined row, and from there the faithful projection and region-read reached the correct region. The force-fit and guessed maps built mismatched pairs, and every downstream read inherited the error. That uniqueness — every consistent source factors through the limit exactly one way — is the universal property that DEFINES a limit. Products, equalizers, and pullbacks are all this same promise.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Only ONE mediating map built a mark-consistent pair, and from there the faithful reads reached the correct grade. The impostor maps built mismatches that poisoned every later read. That uniqueness is the universal property that defines a limit.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Only ONE mediating map built a sigil-consistent pair, and from there the faithful reads reached the correct domain. The impostor maps built mismatches that poisoned every later read. That uniqueness is the universal property that defines a limit.
afterSuccess.abstract: The unique mediating map u : X → L made the cone commute, so the composite reached the goal; non-universal maps broke consistency. Uniqueness of the mediating morphism is the universal property of the limit.

reveal.summary: A limit is defined by a universal property: every consistent cone over the diagram factors through the limit by a UNIQUE mediating morphism. Terminal objects, products, equalizers, and pullbacks are all limits — the single best object completing their shape.
reveal.moreFormal: Reversing every arrow dualises a limit to a COLIMIT: terminal ↦ initial, product ↦ coproduct, pullback ↦ pushout. Same universal-property idea, arrows flipped.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: The most general type that yields all the consistent pieces exactly one way — determined by what maps into it.
